outcome: No new convex uniform 5-polytope has been found or excluded since 26 January 2024, and completeness of the convex case remains unproven; all cataloguing activity found in the window (e.g. the 2024 discovery of 'scab', and count increases from ~1297 to 1333/1348) concerns non-convex uniform 5-polytopes, a broader, related enumeration rather than the stated convex problem.
summary: The stated problem is to determine the complete set of convex uniform 5-polytopes. As of the frozen Wikipedia revision (26 Jan 2024) and still today (checked Sept 2026), this remains unresolved: the known convex examples are two infinite families plus 105 sporadic examples (per the Open Problem Garden entry and en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uniform_5-polytope), all but one (the grand antiprism prism) Wythoffian, and completeness of this convex list has never been proven or disproven. I searched for any 2024-2026 activity specific to the convex case and found none: no new convex uniform 5-polytope announced, no proof of completeness, no disproof via a demonstrated missing case. The activity that does exist in this window — Jonathan Bowers/hi.gher.space community cataloguing (e.g. Mejecide's 2024 discovery of 'scab', the first non-prismatic uniform 5-polytope containing snub cubes, and the running tally rising from ~1297 to figures like 1333 or 1348) — is explicitly about the broader search for *non-convex* (and non-Wythoffian) uniform 5-polytopes outside the infinite families. That is a related but distinct enumeration problem (§3.1): it changes the answer to 'how many non-convex/non-Wythoffian uniform 5-polytopes are known', not to 'what is the complete set of convex uniform 5-polytopes'. I also found and ruled out a 2025 arXiv paper, 'Advancing Geometry with AI: Multi-agent Generation of Polytopes' (arXiv:2502.05199, Świrszcz, Wagner, Williamson et al.), which uses an AI system ('Hopper') to generate novel polytopes for the Hirsch Conjecture, the k-neighbourly polytope problem, and longest monotone paths — none of which is the classification of convex uniform 5-polytopes; it is a different family of polytope problems sharing only the word 'polytope'. No AI system was found anywhere near the convex uniform 5-polytope enumeration itself, which remains a manual/enthusiast-community combinatorial search.
competing_reading: One could argue that since 'scab' and the running tally of non-convex uniform 5-polytopes are literally uniform 5-polytopes, and since any newly found non-Wythoffian example theoretically could turn out to be convex (in principle a non-Wythoffian construction might still yield a convex figure), this cataloguing work is adjacent enough to count as 'progress' on the convex enumeration. But every source describing 'scab' and the tally explicitly frames it as part of the non-convex/general uniform 5-polytope search, and none of the newly catalogued examples are convex; the convex list (105 sporadic + 2 infinite families) has not changed. I therefore classify this as open/no_change_found rather than progress.
what_would_settle_it: Either (a) a published proof that the known convex list (2 infinite families + 105 sporadic examples) is complete, (b) a newly discovered convex uniform 5-polytope not on that list, or (c) a rigorous non-existence argument ruling out further non-Wythoffian convex examples. None of these has appeared as of September 2026.
